data.narrative:
Substrate is a Series A chip and semiconductor company founded by James and Oliver Proud that has raised $100M+. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 8 private-stage peers (including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI) and 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two methods triangulate to a discrete range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $100M raised proxy, implying a $200M valuation consistent with Series A-to-next-stage step-ups. Peer-median anchoring across 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies yields $2.0B, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B (Positron AI, Series B) to $2.3B (Rebellions, Series A). Public-comp anchoring via semiconductor P/S multiples (median 20.4x across the three tickers) is not applicable absent disclosed revenue. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median reflects uncertainty in Substrate's relative maturity and market positioning versus named comparables.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $170M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.1B. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the peer set given frontier-chip heterogeneity, the appropriate stage-progression multiple for this subsector, and unobserved differences in IP, capital efficiency, or customer traction that would justify positioning within the range.
